cf.title: SQL/JSON boolean DEFAULT expression silently replaced with 'false'

input.subject: BUG #19625: SQL/JSON boolean DEFAULT expression silently replaced with 'false'

verdict_reasoning: This is a wrong-result fix in one parser function, and two bug reports show users hit it. The only surviving objection, replication-ondisk-1, is a fixable follow-up about views and rules that keep the stored 'false'::jsonb. It asks for release-note guidance and does not question the fix. A committer who knows the area plans to commit and back-patch it.

brief.title: Fix SQL/JSON boolean DEFAULT ON ERROR/EMPTY replaced by false
brief.problem: When a DEFAULT expression in JSON_VALUE or JSON_QUERY is boolean-valued and the RETURNING type is neither boolean nor integer, the parser replaces it with jsonb 'false' without evaluating it. So DEFAULT true ON ERROR returns false. Any user of SQL/JSON functions with a boolean DEFAULT gets wrong results with no error.
brief.proposed_design: transformJsonBehavior() in parse_expr.c wraps a boolean-valued DEFAULT expression in a to_jsonb() call, so json_populate_type() gets the value the expression actually evaluates to. In v2, Amit Langote keeps the existing jsonb Const for the canned TRUE and FALSE behaviors, so their node tree in back branches does not change.
user_visible_surface: JSON_VALUE and JSON_QUERY with a boolean DEFAULT ... ON ERROR or ON EMPTY return the evaluated value instead of false.
Stored views and rules created before the fix still contain 'false'::jsonb, per the v2 commit message.
author_claims: Non-boolean DEFAULT expressions, and boolean ones with RETURNING boolean or integer, already work correctly.
to_jsonb() handles both canned TRUE/FALSE constants and user-supplied boolean expressions, since there is no bool to jsonb cast.
A reviewer's 40-case test matrix went from 13 to 40 passing, and all nine JSON regression tests passed.
v2 also fixes the cases in bug #19822.
brief.thread_state: Amit Langote posted v2 on 2026-11-12 and says he intends to commit it and back-patch to v17. An AI-assisted review on 2026-10-12 found no blocking issue and asked for more tests, which v2 adds.
unclear: The thread does not say whether release notes will tell users to recreate views and rules that hold the wrong 'false'::jsonb.
The material does not say whether JSON_TABLE column DEFAULT clauses get regression tests in v2, though the reviewer tested JSON_TABLE locally.
The thread does not say how to detect affected stored views after upgrade.

objections.title: Stored views keep the wrong 'false'::jsonb after the fix, with no detection path
objections.failure_scenario: A user has a view with JSON_VALUE(... DEFAULT true ON ERROR) created on 17.x. They install the minor release with the fix, and later use pg_upgrade or dump and restore to move to v20. The view still returns false on error, and the user has no query that finds such views.
objections.argument: Message #5 says views and rules created before the fix keep the wrong 'false'::jsonb in their stored parse tree. The deparsed definition then shows DEFAULT 'false'::jsonb, so pg_dump, pg_upgrade and a physical standby all carry the wrong value forward as if the user wrote it. The fix is back-patched to v17, so many clusters may already hold affected rules. The thread does not say whether the release notes will tell users to recreate these views or how to find them.
objections.author_must_show: Will the release notes give a catalog query that finds affected views and rules, and tell users to recreate them before or after upgrading?

critic.reasoning: Message #5 confirms that views and rules created before the fix keep 'false'::jsonb, and the v2 commit message only records that fact. The thread gives no way to find such views and no advice to recreate them, so this stands as a release-note follow-up.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Stored rules created before the fix keep 'false'::jsonb, and pg_upgrade carries them forward unchanged.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: No catalog change, but stored parse trees in pg_rewrite differ before and after the fix.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The fix changes the result of SQL/JSON DEFAULT ... ON ERROR and ON EMPTY to the evaluated value.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Views created before the fix dump with the stored 'false'::jsonb default, so restore keeps the wrong value.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The committer plans to back-patch to v17; v2 keeps the Const for canned TRUE and FALSE behaviors.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will the release notes tell users to recreate views and rules that were created before the fix and hold the wrong 'false'::jsonb default?
Can the release notes give a catalog query that finds views and rules with a boolean DEFAULT in JSON_VALUE, JSON_QUERY or JSON_TABLE?
Does v2 add regression tests for JSON_TABLE column DEFAULT clauses with a boolean expression?
How does a new view with a boolean DEFAULT deparse after the fix, and does that text restore to the same behavior?

committability.owner_note: Amit Langote posted v2 in the thread and says he intends to commit it and back-patch to v17.
committability.liability: A changed node tree for user-supplied boolean DEFAULT expressions in v17 and later, and the release-note wording for views that keep the old value.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a rebased patch with regression tests one week after the report (message #3).

priority.reason: The fix removes a silent wrong result for users of SQL/JSON functions with a boolean DEFAULT. It touches one function in parse_expr.c, and a committer who knows the area plans to commit it.

provisional_note: Without the code, I could not check how ruleutils deparses the new to_jsonb() wrapper in a dumped view. Messages #4 and #5 were not shown, so the v2 details rest on the brief.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert cascading of JSON_TABLE's ON ERROR
Reverted commit(s): JSON_TABLE PLAN clause
precedents_retrieved.objection:
86ab7f4c721d commit made the table-level ON ERROR clause serve as the default
ON ERROR for columns lacking their own, so that a top-level ERROR ON ERROR
turned per-column evaluation errors into hard errors.

The SQL standard does mandate this cascade, but introducing it should be
a deliberate, separately-documented change, so restore the previous
behavior for now.  This also reverts the paired ruleutils.c logic that
deparsed a column's behavior against an ERROR default: that dropped an
explicit ERROR ON EMPTY from a dumped view, and otherwise emitted a
redundant NULL ON EMPTY.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, Pavel Stehule, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to), and in v2 json_translate, which recursively replaces every value, including array elements, that exactly equals a given string with another string. The author meant it for mapping categorical or enum values deep inside a document, in the style of the Unix tr utility.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan judged blind replacement of every instance of a string, regardless of context, to be a niche use and asked why it could not be an extension. Pavel Stehule suggested using JsonPath to say what to replace, and Peter Eisentraut pointed to json_transform in Oracle and the SQL standard draft, noting that json_transform and json_translate together might confuse users. The thread ends there, and the author later withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Blindly replacing every
instance of a single string regardless of context seems at best a niche
use. Is there any reason not to make this an extension?

precedents_retrieved.title: postgres_fdw: Handle boolean comparison predicates
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Daniel Gustafsson, Ashutosh Bapat, Ronan Dunklau
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes postgres_fdw push the boolean tests IS [NOT] TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN down to the remote server. It deparses each test into an equivalent expression, such as (NOT x OR x IS NULL) for IS NOT TRUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying to HEAD, and the author did not post a rebased version after Daniel Gustafsson asked for one, so it was returned at the end of the commitfest. Ashutosh Bapat and Ronan Dunklau also asked why the tests are rewritten instead of sent as written, and asked for a test on a boolean column. The author did not answer these points.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch no longer applies to HEAD, can you please submit a rebased version?

precedents_retrieved.title: Boolean partition syntax
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the grammar of the partition FOR VALUES clause so that the Boolean literals true and false are accepted as partition bound values, which previously produced a syntax error. Later in the thread a broader alternative was posted that restricts partition bounds to the AexprConst grammar and coerces them during parse analysis.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The discussion moved from the narrow Boolean-literal fix to whether partition bounds should be parsed more generally, for example as expressions evaluated and checked for constancy, and senior developers disagreed with the patch's design. The alternative AexprConst-based patch was not reviewed and was found to reject negative numbers. With the final commitfest in progress and no updated patch, the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Given the current state of this patch, with a number of senior
developers disagreeing with the design, and the last CF being in
progress, I think we should mark this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize JsonbContainerTypeName by reordering type checks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reorders the checks in JsonbContainerTypeName() so that the array and object bit checks run before the scalar check. The author argued that this avoids calling JsonbExtractScalar() in most cases and reported about 0.8% higher tps for jsonb_typeof().
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley argued that one function call cannot change the speed of a whole query by a measurable amount. His test called the function 1 million times and found the patch 3.5% slower, and perf top showed JsonbExtractScalar using little CPU time. Andreas Karlsson added that scalars are not clearly less common, so the new order would slow some workloads while it speeds up others.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It'll amount to a few dozen instructions for the function out of several 10s of millions, when you consider the cost of processing the entire query.

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL/JSON: JSON_TABLE
precedents_retrieved.authors: Fedor Sigaev (sigaev), Alexander Korotkov (smagen), Nikita Glukhov (n.glukhov), Oleg Bartunov (oleg)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds the SQL-standard JSON_TABLE function, including the PLAN clause and PLAN DEFAULT clause, on top of the separate SQL/JSON functions patch set. JSON_TABLE turns a JSON document into rows and typed columns selected by jsonpath expressions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after a rebase in July 2020, and the author did not post a new version within four weeks, so it was returned with feedback. Earlier, Pavel Stehule had marked it ready for committer, after his review objections had been resolved.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Something that has not happened in four weeks, so this is marked
as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow to warn or error on ... = NULL expressions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the transform_null_equals setting from a boolean to an enum with off, warn, error and on values, so that "expr = NULL" expressions can produce a warning or the SQL-standard error. The original patch made 'warn' the default; later versions kept the existing behaviour as the default.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas objected to making 'warn' the default because "foo = NULL" is legal SQL, and saw little value in the warn mode, since such queries can be found with grep. Bruce Momjian considered this one check not useful enough on its own and wanted it to be part of a wider "novice" mode that warns about bad SQL practices. Dmitry Dolgov asked what such a mode should include, received no response, and marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I will again say I would love to see this as part of a wholesale
"novice" mode which warns of generally bad SQL practices.  I don't see
this one item alone as sufficiently useful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improving default column names/aliases of subscript text expressions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the default column name for a subscript expression with a string-literal subscript, such as data['a'] on jsonb, to the subscript value instead of the base column name. A later POC derives the name from the transformed expression and leaves room for type-specific hooks, so subscript implementations could supply their own default alias.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that changing default column names breaks existing queries, and that a GUC to switch the behavior would change query semantics. He was not convinced the new names were better, preferring names like "data_a" if anything changed. He called the transformed-expression POC a single-purpose kluge and suggested that extensible field selection would serve the author's use case better.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix behavior of geo_ops when NaN is involved
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the geometric functions in geo_ops.c handle NaN consistently: boolean operators no longer return true for NaN inputs, and distance functions return NaN. A later version adds tri-state geometric comparisons that return NULL when NaN is involved, with GiST treating NULL as false.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane committed parts of the work in November 2020. The rest was rebased, and a reviewer was asked for comments in March 2021, but no reviewer answered that request or the expanded patch set posted in December 2021. Jacob Champion returned the entry in August 2022 for lack of reviewer interest, and said this was not a rejection.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Rather than code changes, what this patch needs is more community interest.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply a better fix to mdunlinkfork().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Apply a better fix to mdunlinkfork().
Reverted commit(s): Use TRUNCATE to preserve relfilenode for pg_largeobject + index.; Fix failure to remove non-first segments of temporary tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Replace the stopgap fix I made in 0e758ae89 with a cleaner one.

The real problem with 4ab5dae94 is that it contorted this function's
logic substantially, by introducing a third code path that required
different behavior in the function's main loop.  That seems quite
unnecessary on closer inspection: the new IsBinaryUpgrade case can
just share the behavior of the other immediate-unlink cases.  Hence,
revert 4ab5dae94 and most of 0e758ae89 (keeping the latter's
save/restore errno fix), and add IsBinaryUpgrade to the set of
conditions tested to choose immediate unlink.

Also fix some additional places with sloppy handling of errno,
to ensure we have an invariant that we always continue processing
after any non-ENOENT failure of do_truncate.  I doubt that that's
fixing any bug of field importance, so I don't feel it necessary to
back-patch; but we might as well get it right while we're here.

Also improve the comments, which had drifted a bit from what the
code actually does, and neglected to mention some important
considerations.

Back-patch to v15, not because this is fixing any bug but because
it doesn't seem like a good idea for v15's mdunlinkfork logic to be
significantly different from both v14 and v16.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4""
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4""
Reverted commit(s): Change default value of default_toast_compression to "lz4", when available
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 7c1849311e49, due to the fact that more than 60% of
the buildfarm members do not have lz4 installed.  As we are in the last
commit fest of the development cycle, and that it could take a couple
of weeks to stabilize things, this change is reverted for now.

This commit will be reworked in a lighter version, as
default_toast_compression's default can be changed to "lz4" without the
switch from --with-lz4 to --without-lz4.  This approach will keep the
buildfarm at bay, and still allow builds to take advantage of LZ4 in
TOAST by default, as long as the code is compiled with LZ4 support.

A harder requirement based on LZ4 should be achievable at some point,
but it is going to require some work from the buildfarm owners first.
Perhaps this part could be revisited at the beginning of the next
development cycle.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent matches this fix. [P6] reverted unrelated SQL/JSON commits after buildfarm failures, and [P1] reverted a JSON_TABLE ON ERROR cascade that changed behaviour without documentation, so neither recorded reason applies to a wrong-result fix. A committer who knows the area (message #5) plans to commit it. No earlier rejected attempt at this fix appears in the thread or the precedent list.

This fixes a wrong-result bug, a committer owns it, and standard semantics require the evaluated DEFAULT. Stored views keeping 'false'::jsonb after dump or pg_upgrade is a release-note matter, already in the commit message. Not checkable without code: whether new views deparse as an explicit to_jsonb(...) call. Neither precedent's reason applies.

Otherwise the change is parse-time only and uses existing node types. It needs no catversion bump and adds no WAL or protocol change. Older minor versions and standbys can still read the new FuncExpr in stored rules.

The fix has no privilege or exposure aspect. It evaluates a DEFAULT expression the user already wrote and wraps it in the built-in to_jsonb(), bound by OID, so search_path cannot redirect it, and other DEFAULT types already run the user's expression. The fix adds no new privilege, catalog object, default or resource use.

This is a parse-time bug fix in one function, with no hot-path cost, catalog, GUC or API change, and a committer who knows the area plans to commit and back-patch it. Without the code I could not check how ruleutils deparses the new to_jsonb() wrapper in a dumped view. [P1] and [P6] are SQL/JSON reverts whose recorded reasons do not apply to this fix.

This is a wrong-result bug fix inside an existing core SQL/JSON feature, so no existing feature or extension meets the need. The workaround of writing DEFAULT 'true' or using RETURNING boolean only avoids the bug and does not justify keeping wrong results.

This is a wrong-result bug fix, not a feature, so the demand question does not apply. Two independent bug reports (#19625 and #19822) show users hit it, and a committer who knows the area plans to commit and back-patch it.
